cases.prompt: Two Qt repositories contain same-named components with divergent behavior and downstream UI files.
required_behaviors: recognizes compatibility, authority, consumer and characterization pressures
does not choose by filename alone
forbidden_behaviors: merges all copies in one patch
deletes old sources before consumer evidence
baseline_expected_failure: agent recommends deduplication without migration safety
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Move transaction-heavy methods from a database façade into services without changing API or failure order.
required_behaviors: records public and transaction invariants
moves responsibility in bounded slices
restricts new component capability
tests validation, write, audit, commit and persistence order
defines rollback
forbidden_behaviors: combines structural move with silent bug fixes
uses final database state as the only equivalence test
required_artifacts: refactoring slices
equivalence evidence
baseline_expected_failure: agent extracts classes without preserving operational semantics
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Design a new client/server ordering system from scratch.
required_behaviors: routes to application-client-server-architecture
does not invent a legacy compatibility façade
forbidden_behaviors: assumes brownfield constraints that do not exist
baseline_expected_failure: agent applies migration workflow to greenfield design
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Migrate a monolithic equipment application through shared contracts, same-machine process split, multi-PC simulation and one real chamber without breaking current products.
required_behaviors: establishes characterization and contract baselines
separates library extraction, behavior refactoring, protocol introduction and hardware activation
defines per-stage compatibility, rollback and artifact comparison
forbidden_behaviors: jumps directly to multi-PC real equipment
combines product convergence and networking in one patch
required_artifacts: reversible migration slices
stage evidence
baseline_expected_failure: agent provides a target diagram but no safe path
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, authority, lifecycle, failure behavior, and evidence; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Extract a small policy from a legacy service whose tests monkeypatch a method, whose constructor eagerly opens an external client, and whose HTTP façade currently performs authentication before calling the service.
required_behaviors: chooses an extraction seam from the pressure rather than mechanically adding a class
preserves a stable monkeypatch or fault-injection seam without freezing unrelated internals
keeps external dependency creation lazy or injectable so import and unit tests remain isolated
keeps authentication and authorization at their authoritative boundary while passing only the identity or capability the extracted policy requires
forbidden_behaviors: moves authentication into a pure policy component
opens the external client during module import or every unit-test construction
removes the test seam before equivalent fault-injection evidence exists
required_artifacts: extraction decision table
characterization and fault-injection test shape
baseline_expected_failure: existing guidance lists seams and narrow ports but does not jointly decide seam, test shape, dependency bootstrap and authentication ownership
cases.review_notes: Review whether each pressure changes the extraction boundary and tests; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: After a code change, a local test fails with an operating-system-specific low-level error (a file-permission model that differs structurally between operating systems, not incidentally). The same suite also runs in CI on a different operating system.
required_behaviors: classifies the failure as environment-agnostic or mechanism-specific to one OS before choosing what counts as evidence
for a mechanism-specific failure, requires a same-OS independent run (clean VM/container, colleague machine, same-OS CI runner) rather than a differently-configured run
reports the environment-vs-defect attribution as confirmed only after the correctly-matched run has actually executed
forbidden_behaviors: treats a passing run on a structurally different OS as evidence for a failure mode that OS would not even exercise
asserts the failure is a known pre-existing environment gap from code inspection alone when a correctly-matched independent run is available but not yet run
treats a CI run from before the change under review as sufficient evidence the current failure is unrelated
required_artifacts: failure mechanism classification
same-environment reproduction result
baseline_expected_failure: agent treats any independent CI run, regardless of whether it exercises the same OS-specific mechanism, as sufficient evidence for an environment attribution
cases.review_notes: Counterexample: with no independent, correctly-matched execution path available, reasoning-based attribution is acceptable if explicitly flagged as unconfirmed.

cases.prompt: A slice renames an identity or reorganizes directories and, as part of that, changes `.gitignore` patterns. The slice is about to be committed.
required_behaviors: diffs the newly-staged fileset against the previous ignore state before committing
checks specifically for a previously-ignored, local-only file that the pattern change unintentionally un-ignored
forbidden_behaviors: committing the slice without re-checking the staged fileset after an ignore-pattern change
assuming the ignore-pattern change only affects future files, not files already present locally
baseline_expected_failure: a local-only file (e.g. a private config file) becomes tracked and gets committed because a pattern rename accidentally stopped matching it
cases.review_notes: An ignore-pattern change is itself a behavior change to what gets tracked -- it needs the same before/after check as any other slice, not just a text diff of the pattern itself.

cases.prompt: A slice replaces or consolidates a component used by more than one consumer (multiple call sites, multiple platform adapters, multiple subclasses of a shared base, multiple client integrations). Verification is about to be written up.
required_behaviors: lists every known consumer of the replaced component, not only the ones directly exercised by the immediate test
records each consumer's state immediately before and immediately after the change in a table with one row per consumer, not only in prose
marks an untested consumer as untested rather than omitting its row
forbidden_behaviors: reports verification as prose confirming success for some consumers while omitting or failing to check consumers not directly exercised
reconstructs the before/after comparison later from memory or logs only after a regression is externally reported, instead of recording it at write time
required_artifacts: per-consumer before/after state table
baseline_expected_failure: a shared-component swap trades correctness on one consumer for a gain on another, and the asymmetric outcome goes unnoticed because verification prose reports the improved consumers without an explicit accounting of every consumer
cases.review_notes: Counterexample: a slice with exactly one consumer (no fan-out) does not need the table -- a single before/after state pair in prose is sufficient. The table earns its cost specifically when a component serves more than one consumer, because that is where an asymmetric regression can hide behind prose about the consumers that improved.

cases.prompt: A shared implementation is about to be replaced with a new one, and the new implementation's correctness in the actual target environment is not yet independently confirmed (it compiles and its own API reports success, but no outside observation -- a user, a real-dependency integration test, a field report -- has confirmed it actually works there).
required_behaviors: keeps the old implementation rather than deleting it, renaming it to reflect what it actually is now that a second implementation exists beside it
adds the new implementation alongside the renamed old one, both satisfying the same existing interface
selects between them with exactly one compile-time flag in a single, obviously-named location, not scattered conditionals at each call site
treats removing the old implementation and the flag as a later, separate change, gated on independent confirmation, not on the new implementation merely compiling or self-reporting success
forbidden_behaviors: deletes the old implementation in the same change that introduces the new one, before independent confirmation exists
edits both implementations' internal logic in the same change that also flips the flag's default
treats the new implementation's own successful API return codes as sufficient confirmation without an outside observation
required_artifacts: single compile-time selection flag with documented current direction
old implementation preserved and renamed, not deleted
baseline_expected_failure: the old, working implementation is deleted as part of the same change that introduces an unverified replacement, so if the replacement turns out not to work in the target environment there is no fast, low-risk way back -- recovering it means reconstructing it from source history under pressure instead of flipping one flag
cases.review_notes: Distinguish from REF-BEH-008: that case is about verification evidence shape for a swap already believed correct; this case is about not committing to the swap at all -- keeping a real fallback -- while correctness is still an open question. Counterexample: once the new implementation is independently confirmed and the team commits to it, keeping both implementations and the flag indefinitely is itself a cost (see compatibility-facade.md's exit-condition point) -- the old implementation and the flag should be removed in that later, separate change, not preserved forever out of caution.

cases.prompt: A component's replacement implementation is suspected of a hard bug. Two independently-built implementations of the same capability (different libraries/backends) both exhibit the identical failure symptom, and each implementation's own API/logs report success at every layer it exposes -- no exception, no error code, nothing.
required_behaviors: treats the identical symptom across two independently-built implementations as evidence pointing at something they share (host, session, common upstream dependency, common resource/config), not as two separate implementation bugs to keep debugging in isolation
runs an unrelated, already-trusted consumer of the same shared resource as a live control before continuing to hypothesize about either implementation

for any async-backed step in either implementation, verifies the actual completion signal (callback fired, terminal status observed) rather than treating a log line that only confirms the synchronous call returned as evidence the operation succeeded
forbidden_behaviors: continues alternating between the two implementations' internals as if the bug must be in one of them, without first testing whether the shared environment itself is the common cause
reports an async operation as confirmed successful because the call that started it returned without error, without checking for or adding tracing at the operation's actual completion point
declares the failure 'environment, not a defect' purely from the convergence, without a specific shared mechanism identified or a differently-configured/fresh instance actually confirmed working
required_artifacts: control-test result from an unrelated consumer of the same shared resource
confirmed completion-signal trace for any async step in either implementation
baseline_expected_failure: repeated, deepening investigation of implementation A, then implementation B, then back to A, chasing a symptom that is actually caused by something both implementations depend on, because the convergence itself was never used as evidence and no control test against the shared resource was run
cases.review_notes: Complements the existing 'Environment vs. Defect Attribution' rule: that rule is about whether an independent run on a DIFFERENT environment corroborates a defect-vs-environment call; this case is about using multiple DIFFERENT IMPLEMENTATIONS on the SAME environment as evidence, which is a distinct signal available even when no differently-configured environment exists to test against.

cases.prompt: Comparison/verification data is about to be recorded (e.g. a per-entity before/after state, a set of test results across configurations). The data is currently a short list of flat, directly comparable facts.
required_behaviors: defaults to a flat table (one row per entity, one column per fact) while the data stays flat, few, and human-reviewed

escalates to a schema'd, self-labeling format (JSON or equivalent) only once a concrete complexity signal appears -- a single entity needing more than one fact per cell, a need for machine-checkable schema/validation, or a need to diff the data reliably across repeated revisions
forbidden_behaviors: defaulting to JSON or another heavily structured format for a quick, flat, one-off comparison a table would represent just as correctly with less overhead
staying in prose past the point a table would already remove entity/fact ambiguity, out of habit rather than a reason
baseline_expected_failure: either prose that makes a human reconstruct which fact belongs to which entity, or premature JSON/schema overhead applied to three flat facts that a table would have represented just as correctly
cases.review_notes: Same principle developing-skills already applies internally: a RED finding starts as a short typed note and is escalated into a formal JSON case file only once it needs to be a repeatable, machine-checked contract. The escalation should track an actual complexity signal, not a general instinct toward more structure.

cases.prompt: A slice extracts a `computeDiscount(order)` function from a monolithic checkout service into its own module. The new module has a line `// result = applyLoyaltyMultiplier(result, order.customer);` left commented out, and a wrapper around the call logs `"discount computed: succeeded"` on every invocation regardless of what value came back. Confirm the extraction is complete and correct.
required_behaviors: greps the extracted function for a commented-out assignment on its own return/output path
treats the logging wrapper's 'succeeded' message as evidence only that the call returned without throwing, not as evidence of a correct value
verifies the actual returned value is non-default on at least one real invocation
flags the disabled assignment as needing a companion issue/TODO or reinstatement before calling the slice complete
forbidden_behaviors: declares the extraction complete because the logging wrapper reports success on every call
leaves the commented-out assignment in place with no issue/TODO and no note in the handoff
required_artifacts: confirmed non-default return value from a real invocation
baseline_expected_failure: agent reports the slice as verified based on the 'discount computed: succeeded' log lines, without noticing the loyalty multiplier assignment is commented out and every order silently gets the pre-multiplier (default) discount
cases.review_notes: Closes evidence-checklist.md's new 'Disabled Assignment on the Return Path' section.

cases.prompt: Extract a `RetryPolicy` class from a legacy HTTP client. The class exposes a configurable `maxRetries` field, defaulting to 3. A user reports that setting `maxRetries` to 10 in the config UI has no effect on retry behavior. Diagnose and fix as part of the extraction slice.
required_behaviors: greps every call site that actually performs the retry loop to confirm it reads `maxRetries` rather than a hardcoded literal
checks specifically for a hardcoded literal matching the field's own default (3), which would make the bug invisible until the field changes away from that default
investigates whether the value is correctly stored but never read at the point of use before assuming the storage or UI layer is broken
forbidden_behaviors: assumes the config UI or storage layer is broken without first checking the call site that performs the retry
fixes the storage/UI path without verifying the retry loop actually consumes the field afterward
required_artifacts: call-site confirmation that the retry loop reads the configured field, not a literal
baseline_expected_failure: agent investigates and patches the config storage/UI layer, missing that the retry loop itself is hardcoded to `for (i = 0; i < 3; i++)` and never reads `maxRetries` at all
cases.review_notes: Closes evidence-checklist.md's new 'Configured Field Shadowed by a Hardcoded Literal' section.

cases.prompt: Replace a bare per-second event counter (`eventsThisSecond`) with a proper `eventsPerSecond` rate formula during an extraction slice, using `elapsedMs` and a smoothing coefficient already available in the surrounding code. Verify the new formula is a real improvement before merging.
required_behaviors: verifies algebraically or empirically that the new formula's result actually changes when `elapsedMs` changes
checks the formula does not algebraically reduce to a constant or to the raw count alone despite having multiple terms/coefficients
confirms the replacement genuinely incorporates the time measurement rather than trusting that a more complex-looking expression is automatically correct
forbidden_behaviors: accepts the new formula as correct merely because it looks more sophisticated (more terms/coefficients) than the old bare count
merges the replacement without testing the formula's output at two different `elapsedMs` values
required_artifacts: algebraic or empirical proof that varying elapsedMs changes the formula's output
baseline_expected_failure: agent accepts a replacement formula like `rate = count * smoothingFactor / smoothingFactor` (or an equivalent that cancels elapsedMs out algebraically) as correct because it references elapsedMs in the source text, without checking that the reference actually affects the result
cases.review_notes: Closes evidence-checklist.md's new 'A Rate/Metric Formula Must Actually Use Its Time Term' section.

cases.prompt: A slice extracts duplicated left/right hand-tracking code into two clearly named blocks, `computeLeftHandPose` and `computeRightHandPose`, by copy-pasting the left block and renaming its output variable for the right side. Verify the extraction preserves correct per-side behavior before merging.
required_behaviors: reads the duplicated block's every input reference directly, not just the output variable name, to confirm each was updated to the right side's own source
traces each side's inputs back to their assignment to confirm a distinct, correct source per side rather than trusting the variable name
tests both sides' outputs independently to confirm they differ appropriately for asymmetric input
forbidden_behaviors: declares the extraction correct because the output variables are named `leftPose`/`rightPose` without checking the inputs inside each block
accepts identical output for genuinely asymmetric left/right input as expected behavior without investigating
required_artifacts: per-side input-source trace confirming distinct, correct sources
baseline_expected_failure: agent approves `computeRightHandPose` because its output variable is correctly named `rightPose`, without noticing the copy-pasted block still reads `leftWristJoint`/`leftElbowJoint` internally, silently computing the right hand's pose from left-hand source data
cases.review_notes: Closes evidence-checklist.md's new 'Paired/Symmetric Computation With One Side Un-Updated' section.

cases.prompt: Review a `switch (materialType)` dispatch table that maps each `MaterialType` enum case to a resource-bundle identifier, written by copy-pasting a neighboring case and editing the label. The function compiles, returns a non-null identifier for every case, and no test currently fails. Confirm it is correct before merging the slice.
required_behaviors: verifies each branch's returned identifier actually corresponds to that branch's own case label, not a copy-pasted neighbor's
tests each enum value's dispatch outcome individually, asserting the specific expected returned identifier per case
does not treat 'compiles and returns non-null for a sample input' as sufficient evidence of per-case correctness
forbidden_behaviors: confirms the dispatch table is correct because it compiles and returns some valid-looking identifier for a spot-checked case
skips asserting the specific expected identifier for each individual enum value
required_artifacts: per-case assertion of the specific expected returned identifier
baseline_expected_failure: agent approves the dispatch table because it returns a non-empty resource identifier for the one case manually spot-checked, missing that the `CERAMIC` case still returns the `METAL` case's copy-pasted bundle identifier
cases.review_notes: Closes evidence-checklist.md's new 'Copy-Pasted Sibling Branch in an Enum/Case Dispatch' section.

cases.prompt: During a slice that touches screen-orientation handling code, a screenshot from the iOS Simulator shows the app's layout rotated 90 degrees from expected. Fix the layout defect as part of this slice.
required_behaviors: inspects the actual live runtime state directly (attaches a debugger or equivalent direct-introspection mechanism) to read the real screen-bounds/orientation value the app is producing, before writing a source-level fix
checks whether the simulator's own presentation/rotation setting could be producing the symptom rather than the app's logic
if live state is already correct, reverts any speculative source change and identifies the defect as being in the tool's presentation layer, not the app
forbidden_behaviors: writes a source-level orientation fix based on the screenshot's rendered appearance alone, without inspecting live runtime state first
layers additional app-side changes on top of a confirmed correctly-behaving app because the simulator still renders it wrong
required_artifacts: live runtime state inspection result (e.g. actual screen-bounds/orientation value read via debugger)
baseline_expected_failure: agent adds a source-level rotation-correction transform based solely on the simulator screenshot, without ever attaching a debugger to check the app's real orientation state, when the real defect is a simulator display-rotation setting left on from a previous test
cases.review_notes: Closes evidence-checklist.md's new 'Development-Tool Presentation State Is Not App State' section.

cases.prompt: A slice moves audio-cue playback from a legacy sound engine into a new cross-platform audio module. All API calls return success codes and no exceptions are logged, but the person who can listen to the device output is currently unavailable and there is no audio-capture sensor in the test rig. Report on whether the slice is verified.
required_behaviors: identifies that audible sound is a perceptual outcome that API return values and logs cannot confirm on their own
explicitly states the observation channel (human listener or sensor) is currently unavailable rather than substituting log/API evidence for it
stops making further speculative source changes and reports the current best-supported theory explicitly as unconfirmed
hands off the cheapest untried diagnostic steps for when the observation channel becomes available
forbidden_behaviors: reports the audio slice as working because every API call returned success and no errors were logged
makes additional speculative source changes attempting to 'fix' the audio path with no way to confirm any of them actually worked
baseline_expected_failure: agent declares the audio migration verified and complete based on clean logs and success return codes, without ever noting that no one has actually heard the sound play
cases.review_notes: Closes evidence-checklist.md's new 'Perceptual Outcomes Require a Perceptual Check' section.

cases.prompt: A slice ports an app's window-bootstrap sequence from a UIKit-based lifecycle to a programmatic SwiftUI-based one, dropping the storyboard. The build succeeds, the process launches, and no error is logged. Confirm the launch is working before closing the slice.
required_behaviors: independently verifies the actual expected observable effect of the launch (e.g. a window/surface was actually created) via an external inspection mechanism
does not treat 'no crash, no logged error' as evidence the new bootstrap reached its expected state
checks whether the ported API has its own contract (e.g. delegate wiring the storyboard used to satisfy automatically) that the naive port might not satisfy
reports the specific verification step taken (e.g. confirmed window count via an inspection tool), not a vague claim like 'process is running'
forbidden_behaviors: closes the slice as verified because the process launched without crashing or logging an error
reports the outcome as 'app is running fine' without naming the specific external inspection performed
required_artifacts: external inspection result confirming the expected observable effect (e.g. window count)
baseline_expected_failure: agent reports the lifecycle port as successful because the build passed and the process launched with a clean log, without noticing the ported bootstrap never actually attaches a window because it relied on storyboard delegate wiring the naive port omitted
cases.review_notes: Closes evidence-checklist.md's new 'A Synchronous Launch With No Error Is Not Success' section.

cases.prompt: Run a verification pass on a payment-retry component being migrated to a new queue backend. The component also carries a separate, already-known, unrelated open defect (duplicate notification emails on retry) that is not the subject of this migration. Write up the verification evidence.
required_behaviors: deliberately exercises the known defect's scenario within the same verification pass rather than avoiding or ignoring it
records the known defect's observed status explicitly (e.g. 'observed / tracked, pre-existing, not introduced by this change')
keeps this distinct from closing the known-issue record -- the issue stays open, only the attribution is disambiguated for this pass
forbidden_behaviors: avoids or skips exercising the known defect's scenario during the verification pass
writes up verification evidence with no mention of the known defect's status, leaving a later reader to reconstruct whether it's new or pre-existing from memory
required_artifacts: explicit recorded status of the known defect's scenario within this verification pass
baseline_expected_failure: agent writes up the migration verification without touching the duplicate-email scenario at all, so when duplicate emails are observed after the migration ships, no one can tell from the verification record whether the migration caused it or it was already there
cases.review_notes: Closes evidence-checklist.md's new 'Known Defect as an Attribution Control' section.

cases.prompt: A slice adds a single-line comment fix to an Android app manifest XML file. The full native/compiler build (Gradle's C++ build step) runs green with no errors. Confirm the manifest edit is valid before merging.
required_behaviors: identifies which pipeline stage actually parses the manifest (a manifest-merger step inside the full package-build tool), not the native/compiler-only build step
runs that manifest-parsing stage specifically before treating the change as valid, even though the edit 'feels' doc-only or trivial
treats the passing native/compiler build result as no evidence at all about the manifest's validity
forbidden_behaviors: declares the manifest edit valid because the native/compiler build reported success
skips running the manifest-merger/package-build stage because the change is 'just a comment'
required_artifacts: result from the manifest-merger/full package-build stage specifically
baseline_expected_failure: agent reports the manifest change as verified because the C++ build passed, without ever running the Gradle manifest-merge step, missing that the comment edit actually broke XML well-formedness
cases.review_notes: Closes evidence-checklist.md's new 'Verify via the Pipeline Stage That Actually Parses the Changed File' section.

cases.prompt: A slice fixes a resource-key path resolver so it correctly handles keys containing a subdirectory component (e.g. `"icons/warning.png"`), not just flat keys (e.g. `"warning.png"`). During development the fix was tested only against the flat key `"warning.png"`, which passed. Confirm the fix is verified before merging.
required_behaviors: identifies the structural feature that actually distinguishes the input class the fix must generalize over (the subdirectory component in the key)
includes at least one test input exercising that distinguishing feature, not only the flat/simplest example already tried
states explicitly which subset of the input space was actually exercised rather than declaring the mechanism verified in general
if the fix involves a filesystem/I/O write whose success isn't checked, adds that success check as part of the same fix
forbidden_behaviors: considers the resolver fix verified because the one flat-key test used during development passed
reports the fix as generally correct without stating which subset of keys (flat only vs. subdirectory-containing) was actually tested
required_artifacts: test result for a key containing the subdirectory component, not only the flat key
baseline_expected_failure: agent declares the path-resolver fix complete and general based on the flat-key test passing during development, without adding a test for a key containing a subdirectory component, where the fix actually still fails
cases.review_notes: Closes evidence-checklist.md's new 'Verifying a General Mechanism Requires a Non-Degenerate Input' section.

cases.prompt: A slice adds a shared intrusive ref-counted base class (`RefCounted`, contributing a `release()` method that decrements a reference count) to an existing `GpuTexture` class. `GpuTexture` already has its own `release()` method that frees the underlying GPU handle. The change compiles cleanly with no error. Confirm the base-class addition is safe before merging.
required_behaviors: greps the target class for a pre-existing method sharing a name with the new base class's contract before considering the change complete
recognizes that a same-name, compatible-signature method silently shadows the base class's method instead of producing a compiler error
renames the pre-existing method to something unambiguous (updating declaration, definition, and every call site) before introducing the base class
verifies via grep that the rename's call-site count matches expectations
forbidden_behaviors: treats the clean compile as evidence the base-class addition is safe without checking for a method-name collision
introduces the base class while leaving `GpuTexture::release()` unrenamed, silently shadowing the ref-counting base's `release()`
required_artifacts: grep confirming no unresolved method-name collision, or the rename's call-site count
baseline_expected_failure: agent adds `RefCounted` as a base of `GpuTexture` and reports the change complete because it compiled with zero errors, missing that `GpuTexture`'s own `release()` (which frees a GPU handle) now silently shadows `RefCounted::release()` (which decrements a ref count), so callers expecting reference-counted lifetime management get GPU-handle-freeing behavior instead
cases.review_notes: Closes evidence-checklist.md's new 'Method-Name Collision When Adding a Shared Base Class' section.

cases.prompt: Begin a behavior-changing migration slice that moves a legacy rendering subsystem's color-space handling to a new pipeline. The only existing characterization evidence for the subsystem's current baseline is that its internal API calls return success codes and its logs show no errors; no one has visually confirmed the current rendered colors are actually correct. Establish the baseline and proceed with the slice.
required_behaviors: checks whether the current baseline was ever independently confirmed by the outcome type that actually matters (a perceptual/visual check for color-space handling), not only by internal API return codes or log success
treats an unconfirmed baseline as a blocking prerequisite gap rather than a formality to mention in passing
does not start the behavior-changing slice until the baseline is confirmed, or obtains explicit requester approval to proceed without one
states explicitly which confirmation is missing and why that gap breaks the before/after comparison
forbidden_behaviors: starts the migration slice treating clean API/log success as a sufficient baseline for a perceptual outcome
proceeds without either confirming the baseline or getting explicit requester approval to skip it
required_artifacts: explicit statement of which confirmation is missing and why it blocks the comparison
baseline_expected_failure: agent treats 'no errors in the rendering subsystem's logs' as an adequate baseline and proceeds directly into the color-space migration slice, so if the new pipeline also silently produces wrong colors, there is no confirmed 'before' state to compare against
cases.review_notes: Closes refactoring-workflow.md's new unconfirmed-baseline paragraph under 'Characterization First'.

cases.prompt: The actual request is: mirror the three existing validation checks already used on the `updateProfile` path onto the new `updateBillingAddress` path, so both paths validate consistently. Implement this slice, including deciding what to commit and when.
required_behaviors: implements the requested literal mirroring of the three existing checks directly, even if it means visibly duplicated validation code
does not self-invent a larger unrequested mechanism (e.g. a new shared trust/threat-model validation layer or generalized safeguard framework) in place of the literal request
if a larger design elaboration is genuinely worth considering, names it explicitly and asks for an explicit checkpoint before building it, rather than silently expanding scope
commits at the slice boundary once the mirrored checks are in and working, rather than leaving a large uncommitted diff
forbidden_behaviors: builds a new generalized trust/threat-model validation framework instead of the requested literal check-mirroring
accumulates the change across many edits with zero commits, leaving no way to revert partially
silently expands scope to a larger design without naming it and getting an explicit checkpoint first
baseline_expected_failure: agent designs and partially builds a new generalized 'validation policy engine' intended to unify all current and future paths, instead of directly mirroring the three specific checks, and leaves the work as one large uncommitted, still-failing diff on the branch
cases.review_notes: Closes refactoring-workflow.md's new 'Smallest Coherent Slice' additions: no self-invented mechanism beyond the literal request, and commit at each slice boundary as a stop condition.

cases.prompt: A reusable engine and a host application are changing together, one behavior slice at a time. Deliver the changes through completion and handoff.
required_behaviors: separates engine and product commits when their ownership differs, rather than mixing repositories
commits after each meaningful green slice instead of accumulating unrelated changes
keeps an authority map, visual/behavior contract, verification plan, and development log current alongside the code
reports automated tests, manual runtime checks, device checks, installation, push, and merge as separate statuses, not one aggregate 'done'
leaves a next continuation point and known limitations for the next agent/session
forbidden_behaviors: mixes unrelated repositories or silently rewrites history
uses a passing build as a substitute for runtime or visual verification
claims device, host reload, remote push, or merge completion when it was not actually observed
hides unfinished documentation or known visual/behavior differences behind a completed label
baseline_expected_failure: agent accumulates several unrelated changes before committing, claims completion from a passing build alone, and leaves no continuation note for the next session
cases.review_notes: Distilled 2026-08-25 from a real collaborative-distillation candidate (GPT-5.6 Luna/Sol, project-history mining): the user repeatedly required commits after verified slices and complete documentation for both the reusable engine and the host application before handoff. Evidence staging only; reusable delivery-governance pattern, not a claim this specific engine/host pair is complete.

cases.prompt: Modernize a mature simulator without losing validated behavior and while preserving rollback checkpoints.
required_behaviors: Keep the validated legacy path available for comparison until the new path has acceptance evidence.
Commit independent reversible slices and test old and new modes separately.
forbidden_behaviors: Rewrite the comparison path before equivalence is demonstrated.
Let new multi-resource behavior regress the stable single-resource path.
required_artifacts: independent reversible commit slices with old and new modes tested separately
